title: frozen-llm-recommender
description: A Python harness and dataset for evaluating frozen large language models (LLMs) as recommenders of machine-learning pipelines. The harness gives an LLM the anonymized meta-features of a dataset and a catalog of candidate pipelines (OpenML flows), asks it to rank the candidates, parses the returned ranking, and logs every attempt it makes (request and response ids, served model, stop reason, token usage). It talks to Anthropic models and to OpenAI-compatible endpoints (OpenAI, DeepInfra), sends the shared prompt prefix (instructions and catalog) so that it can be cached (explicitly on Anthropic, automatically on OpenAI), asks up to three times when the answer is empty or truncated, and can stop a run at a spending limit. Scoring functions compute normalized regret of a ranking against held-out accuracies, map flows to estimator families, and build leave-one-task-out family portfolios. The repository ships the rankings, ground truth and API logs of the study in the paper "Frozen LLMs as Recommenders for AutoML Pipeline Selection: Can We Trust the Evaluation?" (TAE workshop at NeurIPS 2026), and scripts that reproduce from them Tables 4 and 5 of that paper and, from Tables 1 and 2 the nregret@1 of the eleven LLMs and the three trained baselines, the hit@1 and Spearman of the LLMs, and the differences and p-values against the portfolio, without API keys or OpenML access. It is meant for researchers in AutoML and meta-learning who want to check or extend that evaluation. Reproducing the tables needs Python and the packages in `requirements.txt`; new model runs need an API key and a task pack, which are not included.
